Its protocol trust dependency is the Guardian Network, which Wormhole documents as 19 distributed nodes producing signed VAAs. This is a public, specific description of the provider set for the bridge security model.

The Guardian Network is the protocol?s cross-chain attestation layer: Guardians observe source-chain messages and sign VAAs; destination contracts verify those signatures. It is not an asset-price oracle with per-asset primary/fallback roles.

The documented critical dependency path is Core Contract message publication and verification, the Guardian Network?s VAA attestation, and a destination-chain submitter/relayer. NTT deployments may additionally use configured transceivers and rate limits. No price-feed dependency is documented for Core Bridge verification.

A valid VAA requires the Guardian quorum. The public design describes no secondary trust provider if the 13-of-19 quorum is unavailable, so affected cross-chain delivery waits rather than falling back to an unverified source. NTT rate limits can queue transfers, but do not replace VAA attestation.

If Core Contract verification or Guardian quorum is unavailable, messages cannot be authenticated and cross-chain delivery halts. A relayer outage affects delivery availability, but another actor can submit the publicly available signed VAA. This separates the critical Guardian/Core dependency from the less concentrated delivery dependency.
